title: Database Fundamentals
summary: A database is a managed collection of data with a query language, integrity rules, and a storage engine.

title: Relational Databases
summary: Data as relations (tables), queried with algebra/calculus, constrained by keys.

title: SQL
summary: The declarative language of relational databases: SELECT describes the result, not the plan.

title: Tables
summary: Named relations: a heading of columns and a body of rows. Duplicates depend on whether you mean bag or set.

title: Primary Keys
summary: A column (or set) that uniquely identifies a row. The handle the rest of the schema points at.

title: Foreign Keys
summary: A column that must match a key in another table. Referential integrity as a constraint, not a hope.

title: Constraints
summary: Declarations the engine enforces: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, FK — integrity that survives a bad insert.

title: Joins
summary: Combining rows from two relations by a predicate: inner, left, right, full, cross, and the nested-loop vs hash implementations.

title: Aggregation
summary: GROUP BY, HAVING, and the reduction of many rows to a statistic.

title: Subqueries
summary: A query used as a value, a table, or a predicate. Correlated vs uncorrelated is the performance fork.

title: Indexes
summary: Auxiliary structures (usually B+ trees) that make predicates cheap at the cost of writes and space.

title: Views
summary: Named queries. Virtual by default; materialized when you cache the result.

title: Transactions
summary: A grouping of reads and writes that should succeed or fail as a unit.

title: ACID
summary: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the classical transaction contract.

title: Isolation Levels
summary: Read uncommitted through serializable: which anomalies you tolerate for concurrency.

title: Locks (DB)
summary: Shared/exclusive, row/table, intention locks. Two-phase locking as a correctness argument.

title: MVCC
summary: Readers see a snapshot; writers create versions. Postgres and InnoDB's answer to blocking reads.

title: Database Concurrency
summary: Interleaving transactions without losing integrity. Conflict serializability is the theory.

title: Normalization
summary: Decomposing schemas to remove redundancy. Normal forms are tests, not decorations.

title: 1NF
summary: Atomic values in cells; no repeating groups. The floor of the relational model.

title: 2NF
summary: 1NF plus no partial dependence of a non-key attribute on part of a composite key.

title: 3NF
summary: 2NF plus no transitive dependence of a non-key attribute on the key.

title: BCNF
summary: Every determinant is a candidate key. Stricter than 3NF; sometimes you lose a dependency.

title: Query Optimization
summary: Turning SQL into a cheap plan: statistics, join order, and access paths.

title: Query Planners
summary: Cost-based vs rule-based planners, EXPLAIN, and why the optimizer is the real engine.

title: Storage Engines
summary: The physical implementation: heap files, clustered indexes, InnoDB vs MyISAM vs LSM.

title: Buffer Pool
summary: The database's cache of disk pages. Replacement policy, dirty pages, and checkpoints.

title: Write-Ahead Log
summary: Log the change before the page. Redo/undo, crash recovery, and replication's raw feed.

title: B-Trees
summary: Balanced multiway trees. Internal nodes hold keys and children; used widely in filesystems and DBs.

title: B+ Trees
summary: All values in leaves, leaves linked. The index structure behind almost every relational PK.

title: Replication (DB)
summary: Copying data to other nodes: statement vs row, sync vs async, failover.

title: Sharding
summary: Partitioning rows across machines by a key. Hotspots and resharding are the cost.

title: Partitioning
summary: Splitting a table by range, list, or hash — within one instance or across them.

title: Key-Value Stores
summary: The simplest NoSQL: get/put by key. Redis, Dynamo-style systems.

title: Document Stores
summary: JSON/BSON documents with secondary indexes. Schema-on-read, query-on-fields.

title: Column Stores
summary: Values stored by column, not row. Analytics, compression, and vectorized execution.

title: Graph Databases
summary: First-class nodes and edges. Index-free adjacency and graph query languages.

title: Wi-Fi
summary: 802.11: association, airtime, and a MAC that is nothing like a switched Ethernet.

title: BGP
summary: The internet's inter-domain routing protocol: path vectors, policy, and the default-free zone.

title: OSPF
summary: A link-state IGP: flood LSAs, run Dijkstra, install routes in the RIB.

title: Spanning Tree
summary: A loop-free active topology on a switched LAN. Without it, broadcasts amplify until the LAN dies.

title: fork()
summary: Copy a process: the child gets 0, the parent gets a pid. Copy-on-write makes the copy cheap until a write.

title: Working Set
summary: The pages a process is actually using. If they do not fit in RAM, the system thrashes.
